intro: Hi class — I'm Dr. Chen. I look at earthquake data all day, and the patterns I love most were first noticed by students like yours. Today we'll watch the planet do something it does every day. Then I want every group to tell me what you noticed. There are no wrong answers — just different angles.
act1Post: Every dot you just saw is a real earthquake — magnitude six or stronger, since 1990. Two numbers each: latitude and longitude. Put them all on the same plane and the planet draws something. Don't name it yet. Tell me what you see — every group.
act2Picker: Now you investigate. Different lenses tell different parts of the story. The map shows you where. A histogram shows you the shape of one variable. A scatter shows you whether two variables are related. There's no right lens. Pick what fits the wonderings up there, and write down what each one shows.
act3Top: No answer was wrong. Every group's notice and wonder was a real piece of the picture — even the ones that contradicted each other. Below, you'll see what every group found, side by side. Then I'll show you the science that ties it together.
act3Closing: Thanks for letting me ride along. Every group's notice was a different angle on the same physics — that's how real discovery actually works. The next time you hear about an earthquake on the news, you'll know exactly where on the planet it most likely happened, and why.
